Kamyanka-Buzka New Jewish Cemetery on Shevchenka Street

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Kamianka-Buzka's Jewish community obtained the right to purchase houses and engage in trade in 1589, and to build a synagogue in 1627; in 1837, Sholom Rosenfeld founded a Hasidic dynasty in the town. The Jewish population peaked at 3,549 (43.8 percent) by 1910, reaching an even higher share, 48.4 percent, in 1890. On September 15, 1942, around 1,500 Jews were deported to Bełżec. This cemetery's location remained unknown until 2014, when Meylakh Sheykhet, a contemporary heritage advocate, initiated a court case that successfully uncovered its location using documents otherwise unavailable to the public; no other independent evidence of the site's existence, including on old maps, has since been found.
